title: GPU capacity surface map and order prioritization
summary: Working spreadsheet and prioritization logic for the next 18-week GPU procurement window. Combines on-hand inventory, committed orders, utilization drift, and multi-region lead-time buckets to produce a priority score and recommended order tranche sizing per SKU and region. This is an experimental prioritization surface to help trading-off long-lead SKUs vs short-lead burst lanes.
notes: Purpose: create an actionable order queue that minimizes cross-region disruption and reduces emergency spot leasing. This file focuses on SKU-level decisions (A100 80GB, A100 40GB, H100, L4/L40 equivalents, and a small set of refurbished SKUs) and how to spread orders across APAC/EMEA/NA with staggered lead times. It encodes a simple priority score used by SRE and procurement. Open questions: acceptable risk threshold for single-SKU concentration per region, target utilization floor (currently 58% projected), and whether to convert a portion of monthly demand to short-term leasing in Q1 to reduce long-lead exposure.
assumptions: 1) Weekly burn = 0.85 * forecasted_capacity_demand (includes burst). 2) Committed orders reduce on-hand when they land; pipeline lead times measured in weeks include transit and customs buffer. 3) Regional fallback policy: if a region drops below 4 weeks of burn for 2 consecutive weeks, automatic cascade to short-lead pool is triggered. 4) Refurb units treated as -15% effective capacity for heavy-load inference models.

recommendations: 1) Place Tranche A (high priority, long-lead) orders immediately for APAC H100 and NA H100 to secure arrival in 16-22 weeks. 2) Use Tranche B (medium) to densify EMEA A100-80GB and APAC L4 equivalents staggered across 8-12 week windows to smooth customs risk. 3) Hold Tranche C as monitoring-only: short-lead leasing instead of bulk ordering for A100-40GB and refurb units unless utilization breaks past +12% above baseline. 4) Split each tranche into two shipments where vendor permits to reduce single-shipment customs exposure (example: split 100 -> 60 + 40). 5) Reserve 10% of short-lead budget for emergency market leases during the 6-week window leading up to expected arrivals. 6) Re-run scoring weekly; threshold to trigger emergency lease is priority_score > 50 for any SKU-region and on-hand_weeks < 3.
contingency_lanes: Short-lead market (spot leasing from cloud vendors), cross-region shifting (move burst from NA to EMEA with ~72h notice), and temporary quantization promotion (aggressively quantize suitable models to increase effective capacity by ~8-12%). If customs delays > 4 weeks beyond ETA, escalate to procurement director and activate cross-region fallback.
operational_action_items: - Procurement: issue RFP for Tranche A with three approved vendors; include split-shipment clause. - SRE: add prioritized alert for on-hand_weeks < 4 and apply dynamic routing to lower-cost model variants. - Finance: prepare commit budget for Tranche A and pre-approve a 10% emergency leasing buffer. - Legal: confirm refurbishment warranty terms for used units. - Logistics: validate port/backhaul capacity for APAC arrivals in Jan-Feb.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: SKU concentration on single vendor -> Mitigation: force vendor diversity, 60/40 split across vendors. Risk: customs slow-down in APAC -> Mitigation: stagger arrivals and increase pre-clearance paperwork cadence. Risk: sudden utilization spike from new customer -> Mitigation: burst-to-cloud policy and auto-fallback to lower-capacity quantized model family.
next_steps: 1) Procurement to draft RFP by 2025-10-28. 2) SRE to publish weekly surface map snapshot (automated) by 2025-10-24. 3) Weekly review meeting with procurement/finance/logistics across 6 weeks starting 2025-10-23. 4) Lock Tranche A PO by 2025-11-10.
editorial_notes: This sheet is intentionally compact and operational — treat it as the procurement team's single-pane input for short-term SKU decisions. More granular pricing, vendor lead-time reliability, and customs ETA should live in the procurement CRM; link above. Feedback welcome on weightings in the scoring formula (currently heavier on lead time and utilization delta).
